edges.description: IL-17 and IL-22 drive excessive proliferation and altered differentiation of epidermal keratinocytes in prurigo nodularis lesions.
Neuropeptides (substance P and CGRP) recruit and activate dermal mast cells and eosinophils to degranulate and release histamine, neurotoxins, and nerve growth factor.
Nerve growth factor released by degranulating mast cells and eosinophils promotes dermal nerve fiber sprouting and neuronal hyperplasia.
Neurotoxins, histamine, and NGF released during mast cell and eosinophil degranulation sensitize dermal sensory nerve fibers.
Hyperplastic dermal nerve fibers stimulated by NGF exhibit heightened excitability and sensitization to pruritogens.
Sensitized and activated cutaneous sensory neurons release substance P and CGRP, closing the neuroimmune positive feedback loop.
Neuronal sensitization and hyperexcitability of cutaneous C fibers directly generate severe, intractable pruritus.
Severe pruritus from sensitized cutaneous nerves drives an intractable itch-scratch cycle with repetitive mechanical trauma to reachable skin sites.

evidence.snippet: Neuroimmune dysregulation and chronic scratching are believed to both induce and maintain the characteristic lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Current understanding suggests that a persistent “itch-scratch” vicious cycle, leading to recurrent skin excoriation, crusting, and thickening, is the primary driver of nodule formation ( 3).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Scratching can also lead to increased expression of skin-derived NGF and its receptors ( 97).

nodes.description: Heightened sensitivity and spontaneous excitability of cutaneous C-fiber sensory neurons mediated by cytokines, NGF, periostin, and neuropeptides coupled to upregulated TRPV1 ion channels, lowering the itch threshold, sustaining neuropeptide release, and driving intractable pruritus and repetitive scratching.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Skin neuroimmune interactions and neuronal sensitization play important roles in mediating chronic itch in PN ( 1).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Simultaneously, activated sensory neurons secrete pruritogens such as neuropeptides. On one hand, these neuropeptides act on the neurons themselves to increase their own sensitivity and spontaneous activity; on the other hand, they reciprocally activate immune cells and sustain and amplify inﬂammatory responses, thus promoting chronic itch ( 21).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: TRPV1, also known as the capsaicin receptor, is signiﬁcantly upregulated in nerve ﬁbers and keratinocytes within lesional PN skin ( 127 ).

nodes.description: Activated cutaneous sensory nerve fibers release neuropeptides including substance P and calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) into the dermis, causing vasodilation and further recruitment and activation of dermal inflammatory cells.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Substance P (SP), secreted b y sensory neurons, plays an important role in itch signaling within the peripheral and central nervous systems ( 65, 66).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) is the most abundant neuropeptide in human skin and is often colocalized with SP ( 82).

evidence.reference_title: Prurigo nodularis: new insights into pathogenesis and novel therapeutics.
evidence.snippet: The neuroimmune feedback loop in PN involves neuropeptides released from nerve fibres that cause vasodilation and further recruitment of inflammatory cells.

nodes.description: Cutaneous and systemic type 2 helper T-cell (Th2) activation with increased expression of IL-4, IL-13, and IL-4 receptor alpha in prurigo nodules and elevated circulating IL-13. IL-4 (primarily from T lymphocytes and basophils) and IL-13 (primarily from eosinophils) directly activate and sensitize itch-sensitive neurons via IL-4Ralpha, recruit eosinophils and mast cells, and promote dermal fibroblast proliferation and extracellular matrix synthesis.

evidence.reference_title: Prurigo nodularis: new insights into pathogenesis and novel therapeutics.
evidence.snippet: There is a role for type 2 inflammation in PN in addition to T-helper (Th)17 and Th22-mediated inflammation.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: The expression of IL-4, IL-13, and IL-4 receptor (IL-4R) is upregulated in prurigo nodules, with IL-4 correlating with the intensity of itch ( 8, 11, 26, 27). IL-4 is primarily expressed in T lymphocytes and basophils, whereas IL-13 is primarily expressed in eosinophils (26). Studies have shown that IL-4 and IL-13 activate itch-sensitive neurons in both humans and mice through IL-4R a (28).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: In addition, IL-4 and IL-13 exert pruritogenic effects by recruiting eosinophils and mast cells, driving IgE synthesis, and interacting with IL-31 ( 30 ). They promote ﬁbroblast proliferation, differentiation, and synthesis of extracellular matrix proteins such as periostin in the dermis, mediating PN-associated skin ﬁbrosis and itch (20).

nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody targeting IL-4 receptor alpha (IL-4Ralpha) that blocks IL-4 and IL-13 signaling; the first FDA- and EMA-approved systemic therapy for adult patients with prurigo nodularis, demonstrating significant reductions in worst-itch scores in the phase 3 PRIME and PRIME2 trials.

evidence.reference_title: Prurigo nodularis: new insights into pathogenesis and novel therapeutics.
evidence.snippet: The only drug currently approved for PN in the USA and Europe is dupilumab, an IL-4Rα inhibitor that blocks signalling through IL-4 and IL-13, which is undergoing post-marketing surveillance.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Based on two phase 3 clinical trials, dupilumab (an IL-4R a monoclonal antibody simultaneously antagonizing IL-4 and IL-13) has become the ﬁrst the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)/European Medicines Agency (EMA)/China National Medical Products Administration (NMPA)-approved treatment for adult patients with PN. C ompared to placebo, signi ﬁcant improvements in weekly average worst itch numeric rating scale (WI-NRS) with dupilumab were observed as early as week 3 in PRIME and week 4 in PRIME2 ( 134).

nodes.description: Excessive proliferation and altered differentiation of epidermal keratinocytes in lesional prurigo nodularis skin driven by chronic scratching and IL-17, IL-22, and IL-31 signaling, producing marked epidermal hyperkeratosis overlying the dermal nodules.

nodes.description: Epidermal thickening and hyperkeratosis overlying the pruritic dermal nodules on the trunk and extremities.

evidence.snippet: Prurigo nodularis (PN) is a chronic neuroimmune skin disease characterized by bilaterally distributed pruritic hyperkeratotic nodules on extremities and trunk.

nodes.description: Markedly elevated lesional and serum IL-31 (secreted primarily by Th2 cells and dermal CD11c+ myeloid dendritic cells) and upregulated IL-6 and MAPK12 signal through heterodimeric IL-31RA/OSMRB receptors and the JAK1/STAT3/STAT6 pathway in lesional skin. IL-31/IL-31RA signaling promotes sensory nerve axon sprouting, sensitizes pruriceptive neurons, and drives downstream keratinocyte proliferation and profibrotic fibroblast responses.

evidence.snippet: The upregulation of IL-6, MAPK12, and IL-31 further supported neuroimmune dysregulation in PN.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: IL-31 is mainly secreted by Th2 cells, and dermal CD11c + myeloid dendritic cells are an important source of IL-31 in PN ( 33, 34).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: In PN lesions, this receptor is also notably increased, and the intensity of pruritus in PN is closely related to the number of IL-31+ cells and IL- 31Ra+ cells in the dermis ( 33). IL-31 promotes sprouting of skin sensory nerve axons and enhances their sensitivity to pruritogens (41, 42).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Several key cytokines, such as IL-4, IL-13, IL-31, and OSM, play roles in propagating pruritus and in ﬂammation in PN through the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, particularly involving JAK1, STAT3, and STAT6 ( 28, 45, 108).

nodes.description: Dermal mast cells and eosinophils aggregate in close contact with peripheral sensory nerve endings, degranulate, and release neurotoxins, histamine, and nerve growth factor (NGF) into the dermal microenvironment.

evidence.reference_title: Prurigo nodularis: new insights into pathogenesis and novel therapeutics.
evidence.snippet: Inflammatory cells, particularly mast cells and eosinophils, degranulate and release neurotoxins, as well as nerve growth factor, which may contribute to the neuronal hyperplasia seen in the dermis of patients with PN and neural sensitization.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Notably, mast cells and eosinophils often aggregate around the peripheral sensory nerve endings, establishing close contact with them ( 15– 17).

nodes.description: Elevated nerve growth factor (NGF) signaling through upregulated TrkA and p75NTR receptors on cutaneous nerve fibers drives sprouting of afferent nerves and increased density of itch-sensing nerve fibers in the dermis, accompanied by reduced intraepidermal nerve fiber density.

evidence.reference_title: Prurigo nodularis: new insights into pathogenesis and novel therapeutics.
evidence.snippet: Neural dysregulation in PN features a lower density of itch-sensing nerve fibres in the epidermis (upper layer of the skin) and a higher density of itch-sensing nerve fibres in the dermis (lower layer of the skin).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: NGF is a neurotrophic factor that primarily activates, sensitizes, and sprouts skin nerve ﬁbers, promoting the release of neuropeptides, such as SP and CGRP ( 96, 98).

nodes.description: Monoclonal antibody targeting the IL-31 receptor A (IL-31RA) that blocks IL-31-driven pruritus, significantly reduces peak pruritus and skin lesion severity in randomized clinical trials, and reverses pathological COL11A1+ fibroblast and keratinocyte transcriptional responses in prurigo nodularis skin.

evidence.reference_title: Trial of Nemolizumab in Moderate-to-Severe Prurigo Nodularis.
evidence.snippet: Nemolizumab resulted in a greater reduction in pruritus and severity of skin lesions than placebo in patients with prurigo nodularis but was associated with adverse events.

evidence.reference_title: Prurigo nodularis: new insights into pathogenesis and novel therapeutics.
evidence.snippet: The anti-IL-31 receptor A inhibitor nemolizumab is in late-stage development with positive phase III data reported.

evidence.snippet: This study further shows the broad effect of nemolizumab on PN cell types, with a prominent effect driving COL11A1+ fibroblast and keratinocyte responses toward normal.

nodes.description: Expansion and activation of profibrotic papillary dermal COL11A1+ fibroblasts and POSTN+WNT5A+ myofibroblast/cancer-associated fibroblast-like subclusters, accompanied by upregulation of MMP14, COL6A3, TGFBR1, and dermal periostin deposition, which distinguish prurigo nodularis from atopic dermatitis, drive nodular dermal fibrosis, and further stimulate itch-sensing nerve fibers.

evidence.reference_title: Single-cell profiling of prurigo nodularis demonstrates immune-stromal crosstalk driving profibrotic responses and reversal with nemolizumab.
evidence.snippet: This study demonstrates that PN is an inflammatory skin disease characterized by both keratinocyte proliferation and activation of profibrotic responses. This study also demonstrates that the COL11A1+ fibroblast subset is a major contributor to fibrosis and is predominantly found in the papillary dermis of PN skin. Activation of fibrotic responses is the main distinguishing feature between PN and atopic dermatitis skin.

evidence.reference_title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Dysregulated POSTN+WNT5A+ Fibroblast Subclusters in Prurigo Nodularis.
evidence.snippet: Lesional PN has increased dysregulated fibroblasts (FBs) and myofibroblasts. FBs in lesional PN were shifted toward a cancer-associated FB-like phenotype, with POSTN+WNT5A+ cancer-associated FBs increased in PN and similarly so in squamous cell carcinoma.

evidence.reference_title: Nanostring Transcriptomic Analysis Highlights IL-6 Family and TGF-β Pathways in the Pathogenesis of Prurigo Nodularis.
evidence.snippet: MMP14, COL6A3, and TGFBR1 were highly upregulated in PN, reflecting an active fibrotic process.

evidence.snippet: Prurigo nodularis (PN) is an inflammatory skin condition characterized by intensely pruritic nodules on the skin. Patients with PN suffer from an intractable itch-scratch cycle leading to impaired sleep, psychosocial distress and a significant disruption in quality of life.

evidence.reference_title: Prurigo nodularis: new insights into pathogenesis and novel therapeutics.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Previous studies have shown an increased expression of IL-17 in lesional PN skin, coupled with an increase in the number of Th17 cells within the lesions ( 9, 27, 49).

evidence.reference_title: Molecular mechanisms of pruritus in prurigo nodularis
evidence.snippet: Several studies have shown that the expression of the Th22 cell cytokine IL-22 is elevated in pruritic PN lesions, which is potentially associated with impaired epidermal proliferation and differentiation and skin in ﬂammation ( 27, 51).
